prompt: A graph-colouring SAT encoding requires exactly one of three colours at every vertex, but accidentally omits all edge constraints. What can go wrong?

options.explanation: The at-least-one clause at each vertex still prevents this.

options.text: Every vertex must receive all three colours
options.explanation: The at-most-one clauses prevent multiple colours.

options.text: The solver may accept adjacent vertices with the same colour
options.explanation: Correct. No remaining clause connects the colour choices at the two ends of an edge.
Removing constraints allows more assignments; it cannot make a previously satisfiable instance unsatisfiable.

workedExample: At-least-one clauses prevent an uncoloured vertex, at-most-one clauses prevent several colours on a vertex, and edge clauses prevent equal colours at adjacent vertices. Omitting the edge family admits assignments that obey each vertex's rules yet are not graph colourings.
